title: The Eurosystem's comprehensive payments strategy
date_evidence: The Eurosystem published its comprehensive payments strategy on 31 March 2026, extending its prior retail payments work to cover wholesale, business-to-business and cross-border payments.
key_claim: The share of SCT Inst (instant) transactions in the total volume of credit transfers rose to almost 34% in the fourth quarter of 2025; more than two-thirds of euro area card-based transactions are processed based on the business rules set by non-European companies, and 13 euro area countries depend on international card schemes or mobile solutions for in-store payments; the strategy frames the digital euro and private European card and account-to-account (A2A) schemes as coexisting, and notes the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation (PSR) and PSD3 might further support the uptake of A2A payment initiation solutions based on instant payments; the Governing Council aims to be ready to issue the digital euro in 2029.
frame_summary: The ECB argues Europe must reduce its dependence on non-European payment rails by promoting instant payments, A2A initiation and a digital euro as a sovereign alternative to international card schemes.
notes: Tier 1 central bank strategy. Anchor for the European payments-sovereignty and instant-payments-as-A2A-enabler strand. Published 31 March 2026 (confirmed via ECB press release pr260331 announcing the strategy).

title: Review of Merchant Card Payment Costs and Surcharging - Conclusions Paper (Interchange Fees)
key_claim: The Payments System Board concluded it is in the public interest to lower the cap on domestic-issued consumer credit card interchange to 0.3 per cent and abolish the benchmark, lower the debit and prepaid cap to 8 cents (or 0.16 per cent ad valorem), and introduce a single cap of 1.0 per cent on interchange for all foreign-issued card transactions; cash use has declined from around 70 per cent of consumer payments by number in 2007 to 15 per cent in 2025; submissions noted the higher prevalence of account-to-account payment methods for B2B transactions, and it is common practice for merchants to offer similar payment terms for commercial credit cards and account-to-account payments.
frame_summary: The RBA is moving to cut card interchange caps and ban surcharging because cards now dominate a near-cashless economy, while noting account-to-account methods are already an alternative in business payments.
notes: Tier 1 regulator conclusions paper. Quantifies the regulatory squeeze on card interchange and positions A2A as an emerging alternative; adds Australian geographic breadth. Created 2026-03-31, last modified 2026-06-19.

title: Instant Payments Regulation
date_evidence: Evergreen ECB explainer page on the Instant Payments Regulation; no single article publication date on page.
key_claim: Under the EU Instant Payments Regulation, euro-area payment service providers must be able to send and receive instant euro credit transfers, may not charge more for an instant transfer than for a standard credit transfer, and from 9 October 2025 must offer payers a free Verification of Payee service that checks the payee name against the IBAN before a transfer is authorised.
frame_summary: The ECB explains that the Instant Payments Regulation makes real-time euro transfers a mandatory, low-cost, safety-checked baseline across the euro area.
notes: Tier 1 evergreen regulatory reference. Establishes the mandatory instant-payments rail and price/fraud protections that make A2A viable at point of sale.

title: 2026: the year of European sovereignty in payments?
date_evidence: Eco Week January 26, 2026 ... 2026: the year of European sovereignty in payments? 01/26/2026
key_claim: Two-thirds of digital payments in the Eurozone rely on non-European providers, mainly American; sovereign payment solutions are available in 14 EU countries representing 77% of the population, while in 13 countries there is no alternative to International Card Schemes; 2026 could be the year a European alternative takes off and reaches critical mass.
frame_summary: BNP Paribas argues 2026 may be the inflection year when a European payments alternative to international card schemes finally reaches critical mass.
notes: Tier 2 bank economic-research editorial. Structural anchor (3-6m band) for the European sovereignty framing; cited inline like any other source.

title: Commercial VRP & UKPI (2026): The UK Payments Initiative Explained
date_evidence: LIVE - WAVE 1 Last reviewed: June 8, 2026 ... UKPI's commercial VRP scheme went live on 2 June 2026 - the UK's first new payment scheme since Faster Payments in 2008.
key_claim: The UK Payments Initiative (UKPI) commercial Variable Recurring Payments scheme went live on 2 June 2026, described by regulators as the UK's first new payment scheme since Faster Payments launched in 2008; it was established by 31 funders spanning banks, card networks and open banking fintechs, targets around 75% of UK current-account coverage at launch, and uses a capped, centrally managed pence-per-transaction fee intended to be fixed for roughly five years (with a modelled bank cost around GBP 0.02 per transaction); commercial VRP extends VRP from me-to-me sweeping to paying real businesses and is positioned to replace Direct Debit and card-on-file.
frame_summary: Open Banking Tracker documents that the UK now has its first new payment scheme in 17 years, giving account-to-account payments a commercial rulebook to compete with Direct Debit and card-on-file.
notes: Tier 3 specialist tracker/aggregator. Maintained guide, last reviewed 8 June 2026; cites the FCA 2 June 2026 launch statement. Source for the UK cVRP/UKPI scheme strand.

title: Visa, Mastercard fend off fee foes
date_evidence: meta-article_date_original: Monday, June 22, 2026, 10:45 AM ; Published June 22, 2026
key_claim: Despite state legislation and a federal court settlement aimed at curbing card fees, the card networks and their issuers prevailed in the first half of 2026: a Colorado bill to rein in fees was vetoed, an Illinois interchange-fee law was twice postponed amid federal litigation, the Credit Card Competition Act again failed to pass Congress, and a renegotiated Visa-Mastercard merchant settlement was approved over objections; a Federal Reserve proposal to cut debit fees has been slow to take effect.
frame_summary: Payments Dive argues that, so far in 2026, Visa and Mastercard have successfully beaten back legislative and legal attempts to cut their interchange and network fees.
notes: Tier 3 trade journalism. Counter-argument anchor: the card fee model is proving resilient to direct regulatory and legal attack in the US.

title: Global Payments Report 2026
date_evidence: meta-article:published_time: 2026-04-08T12:08:13+00:00 ; 1st April 2026 - Worldpay, now Global Payments (NYSE: GPN), released its 11th annual Global Payments Report (GPR)
key_claim: In Hong Kong, account-to-account (A2A) payments already represent 19% of e-commerce and 9% of point-of-sale transaction value in 2025, forecast to reach 23% of e-commerce and 13% of POS by 2030; in Thailand the government's PromptPay instant network drove 44% of online and 43% of in-person spend in 2025; interconnected real-time networks across Singapore (PayNow), Thailand (PromptPay) and Malaysia (DuitNow) are providing an alternative to global credit card networks.
frame_summary: Worldpay's report shows account-to-account payments are already a large and growing share of spending in several Asian markets, where interoperable instant networks act as an alternative to global card schemes.
notes: Tier 4 vendor research (Worldpay/Global Payments), used as directional corroboration of A2A scale in Asia, not as anchor. Press release carried on Treasury Today; report published 1 April 2026.
